seoTitle: Entitlement Qualification Lifecycle Journey Example
seoDescription: See how a journey decides whether a right actually exists, keeping granted, denied and pending apart from being eligible or having paid toward it.

seoTitle: From Entitlement Grant to Working Access: Journey Map
seoDescription: A journey that holds the gap between granting a right and the thing behind it working, with provisioning steps, waits and an availability check.

seoTitle: How Entitlement Scope Changes Expand or Reduce Rights
seoDescription: Model how a scope change applies only the difference between old and new rights, instead of re-applying a whole scope over one that already works.

seoTitle: Entitlement Loss: Revoke Access, Reconcile Commitments
seoDescription: Examine a journey that stops future use of an ended right while leaving what was validly created intact, and hands off what still depends on it.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to ACC-80, which also models ending a capability with dependency and obligation reconciliation.

seoTitle: Authorization Checks at the Moment of Access Attempt
seoDescription: A decision journey run at the moment of the attempt, weighing whether one actor may take one action on one resource, and where a step-up leads next.

seoTitle: Credential Lifecycle Journey from Issue to Revocation
seoDescription: Follow an access artifact through its own validity lifecycle, from issue and activation to use, expiry or revocation, apart from the right it stands for.

seoTitle: Credential Revocation and Replacement Journey Example
seoDescription: How a compromised credential is taken out of use immediately, while any replacement is issued only through its own separately authorised path.

seoTitle: Access Suspension and Restricted State Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: A journey that restricts a defined capability scope for a stated reason, keeps restoration genuinely possible, and holds a timed route to termination.

seoTitle: Revalidating Capabilities Before Access Is Restored
seoDescription: Rebuild access from what is currently valid rather than replaying an old capability set. Examine the revalidation checks and the exits each one can take.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to ACC-78, whose restore exit covers the same restoration decision this journey models in full.

seoTitle: Deprovisioning Journey: Dependency Check Before Removal
seoDescription: Model removing a capability that is no longer authorised only after confirming nothing still depends on it, with retain, escalate and handoff branches.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to ACC-74, which also models removing capability after an entitlement ends.

seoTitle: Anonymous Intent to Qualified Entry Journey Example
seoDescription: Carry an anonymous intent signal through identity resolution without inventing an identity, then treat lifecycle entry as a separate question to answer.

seoTitle: Captured Interest Routing: Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: A router journey that sends first-party interest to the destination its own content justifies, rather than filing every capture as a lead or a subscriber.

seoTitle: Intent Escalation Journey: Handoff to Higher Intent
seoDescription: Move ownership when someone in a low-intent lifecycle does something that no longer fits it, and see how the journey left behind is made to go quiet.

seoTitle: High-Intent Action Routing: Human or Automated Path
seoDescription: After a commercially serious act, decide whether the next step needs a person's judgement, resolving what already exists before anything new is created.

seoTitle: Qualification State Change Routing and Re-entry Rules
seoDescription: Treat qualification as a reversible state and route by the reason it changed, not by a label applied once. Includes re-entry limits and timed exits.

seoTitle: Dynamic Eligibility Re-decided as Underlying Data Changes
seoDescription: Re-evaluate eligibility whenever the underlying data changes, and keep what losing it forbids next separate from what it does not undo retroactively.

seoTitle: Intent Decay Journey: De-prioritise, Cool Down or Exit
seoDescription: Let a recorded high-intent state expire once the evidence behind it goes stale, with cooldown and exit paths instead of pursuit built on one old action.

seoTitle: Commercial Destination Reached: Acquisition Suppression
seoDescription: Once the outcome acquisition existed to cause is recorded, this journey gives up ownership, stops what it already queued and hands the person onward.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to ACT-16, which also models a journey releasing ownership and cancelling queued messages on an authoritative outcome.

seoTitle: Bounded Lead Education Journey Before Progress or Sunset
seoDescription: Give a valid but not-yet-ready lead a fixed window of useful education, then close the journey on a defined boundary whether or not the window worked.

seoTitle: Routing Commercial Declines by Their Underlying Reason
seoDescription: Route a negative commercial outcome by its actual cause, with terminal, cooldown and recycle branches instead of filing every one of them under lost.

seoTitle: Onboarding Route Selection: Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Choose the onboarding path from the work that is genuinely required to reach value, decided up front before any of that setup work actually begins.

seoTitle: Onboarding Progress Journey and the Next Setup Step
seoDescription: Advance onboarding from the state the setup record actually reports, one useful step at a time, until activation happens or the window closes.

seoTitle: Resolving a Named Activation Blocker Before Resuming
seoDescription: Point a whole journey at a single named missing requirement, then resume onboarding once it exists, with escalation and exit paths if it never does.

seoTitle: Detecting a Struggling User and Offering Assistance
seoDescription: Detect someone visibly trying without getting anywhere, offer help, and stop asking once they have answered. See the recovery and exit branches in full.

seoTitle: First Value Milestone: Recognition and Next Action
seoDescription: Mark the moment the product first did something real for a person, and then point at whatever naturally follows on from that particular milestone.

seoTitle: When Activation Stops Onboarding and Hands Off Adoption
seoDescription: Make onboarding let go the moment activation is recorded, including the messages it already queued, and pass ownership on to the adoption journey.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to ACQ-08, which also models suppression and handoff the moment the target outcome is recorded.

seoTitle: Early Adoption to Stable Use: Lifecycle Journey Map
seoDescription: Carry an account from producing value once to producing it repeatedly, measured against its own use-case rather than one shared usage threshold.

seoTitle: Diagnosing an Adoption Stall Before Acting On the Cause
seoDescription: Work out why value stopped recurring before doing anything about it, including the case where nothing is wrong at all, then recover or re-route.

seoTitle: Role and Use-Case Discovery Journey for Onboarding
seoDescription: Ask for the one piece of context onboarding needs, only when not having it would genuinely change the path, then adapt the route to the answer given.

seoTitle: Dormant Non-Customer Reactivation Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: One bounded attempt to restart a relationship that never became a paying one, judged on what the person actually did, then re-qualified or closed out.

seoTitle: Deciding a Communication Obligation Before Any Message
seoDescription: Decide whether anyone is genuinely owed a message about a business event, before any message exists, with suppression as a first-class outcome.

seoTitle: Communication Recipient Resolution: Ready, Hold or Fail
seoDescription: Establish who is actually owed a communication and where they can currently be reached, with hold and failure paths for when no destination resolves.

seoTitle: Communication Permission and Preference Check Journey
seoDescription: Decide whether a working destination may carry this particular message, given what the message is for, with allow, suppress and alternate outcomes.

seoTitle: Choosing the Channels a Communication Obligation Needs
seoDescription: A router journey that picks the smallest set of channels which actually satisfies the obligation, then builds the message for the ones it selected.

seoTitle: Revalidating a Prepared Message Just Before It Is Sent
seoDescription: Check that a prepared message is still true immediately before it goes out, and stop the send when the state it describes has moved on since preparation.

seoTitle: Send Attempt Journey: Accepted, Failed or Unknown State
seoDescription: Record what happened when a message was handed to a provider, which is not the same as what happened to the recipient. The unknown state is modelled too.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to CMS-207, which also resolves accepted, failed and unknown states for the same delivery attempt.

seoTitle: Deriving the Real Delivery Outcome from Channel Reports
seoDescription: Derive the real delivery state from what the channel reports, attached to the exact attempt it concerns, then update the communication it belongs to.
reviewReason: Near-identical in subject to CMS-206, which also records the accepted, failed or unknown state of a delivery attempt.

seoTitle: Message Delivery Failure and Retry Journey Example
seoDescription: What should happen when a message fails to reach its destination? This flow classifies the failure and decides between a retry, a fallback or a full stop.

seoTitle: Communication Obligation Closure and Escalation Map
seoDescription: Models how a communication obligation is closed once delivery attempts reach an outcome, and how the cases that could not be met are escalated instead.

seoTitle: Capturing Permission With an Explicit Scope Record
seoDescription: How a permission decision becomes an auditable record of what was authorised, by purpose, channel and scope. Follow the validate, activate or reject path.

seoTitle: Communication Preference Capture Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Shows how a declared preference is recorded and used to personalise permitted communication, in a store built so preference can never become permission.

seoTitle: Preference Change Recalculation Customer Journey
seoDescription: When someone changes a preference, what happens to messages already queued? This flow recalculates active journey instances and suppresses or adapts each.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-34, which also models a preference change triggering a recalculation; CON-33 covers preferences in general and CON-34 covers frequency only.

seoTitle: Communication Frequency Change Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Examine how a frequency preference recalculates the cadence of optional messaging, applies prospectively and leaves required messages untouched.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-33, the general preference-change recalculation journey; this record is the frequency-specific case.

seoTitle: Consent and Permission Change Enforcement Journey
seoDescription: A permission change has to stop affected communication at once. This journey models immediate enforcement first, then propagation to the other systems.

seoTitle: Channel Contactability and Reachability Journey Map
seoDescription: Tracks whether a channel can still reach a person, separately from whether it may, holding route health per contact point so sending avoids what is broken.

seoTitle: Communication Suppression State Journey Example
seoDescription: Every reason a message is not sent becomes an explicit, scoped, releasable state. Review how a suppression opens, is re-evaluated and is finally released.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-39, which also holds messaging back; CON-38 records any suppression reason as state while CON-39 is a time-bound cooldown on optional messaging.

seoTitle: Messaging Cooldown and Re-evaluation Journey Map
seoDescription: Models a temporary hold on optional messaging after a trigger: how the cooldown is scoped, when it is re-evaluated and why permission stays intact.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-38, the general suppression-state journey; this record covers the time-bound cooldown case only.

seoTitle: Permission Conflict and Fail-Safe Hold Journey
seoDescription: When two systems disagree about permission, optional messaging stays closed. Follow the fail-safe hold, evidence-based reconciliation and restore path.

seoTitle: Establishing Entity Ownership With an Explicit Act
seoDescription: How an accountable owner is established by an explicit act rather than inferred. The flow validates the requesting authority, then assigns or rejects it.

seoTitle: Ownership Transfer Request and Validation Journey
seoDescription: Proposing a future controller without disturbing the one an entity currently has. See how the request is validated, left pending acceptance, or rejected.

seoTitle: Ownership Transfer Acceptance and Revalidation Map
seoDescription: An acceptance made today must still match the transfer proposed. See how the request version is revalidated and then executed or allowed to expire.

seoTitle: Ownership Cutover Without an Uncontrolled Entity
seoDescription: Moving control between two parties while the entity is never left uncontrolled. Follow the new owner assignment and the reconciliation of the old one.

seoTitle: Granting Scoped Authority on an Owner's Behalf
seoDescription: Letting somebody act on an owner's behalf inside a boundary, without moving anything. Review how the scope is defined and the grant issued or refused.

seoTitle: Temporary Delegation Expiry and Renewal Journey Map
seoDescription: Borrowed authority has to end at its boundary. This flow checks the boundary still belongs to a delegation that exists, then revokes, extends or restores.

seoTitle: Delegation Revocation and Retained Access Journey
seoDescription: Taking back exactly what was lent and nothing else. The journey removes capabilities that exist because of the delegation, preserving independent access.

seoTitle: Protecting an Entity When Its Owner Is Unavailable
seoDescription: What holds an entity safely when its owner cannot act? This flow protects the ownership state and works towards recovery rather than the nearest party.

seoTitle: Data Intake, Format Detection and Parsing Journey
seoDescription: How a submitted dataset is identified, parsed and brought into a stable readable form, or rejected, before anything real is touched. Follow each branch.

seoTitle: Schema and Semantic Data Validation Journey Map
seoDescription: Checks parsed data against the target's schema and business rules, record by record, then accepts, rejects or quarantines it. Examine every branch here.

seoTitle: Impact Preview and Approval Before a Data Change
seoDescription: Before a mutation runs, what would it actually do? This flow builds the impact preview so approval attaches to real effects, then confirms or holds it.

seoTitle: Idempotent Import Execution and Record Outcomes
seoDescription: Applies a frozen, validated change set to production state and keeps every record's outcome. See how complete, partial and failed results are separated.

seoTitle: Partial Import Recovery and Resume Journey Example
seoDescription: Only the records that did not land should be touched again. Follow how the failed scope is isolated, corrected and resumed without disturbing the rest.

seoTitle: Migration Readiness and Source-to-Target Mapping
seoDescription: Proving the target can carry the source's meaning before anything moves. Review the source-to-target mapping and the readiness checks that gate the plan.

seoTitle: Migration Execution and Population Verification
seoDescription: Moves the population into the target, then proves the result still means what the source meant. Examine the copy, transform and verification steps.

seoTitle: System Cutover, Observation and Rollback Journey
seoDescription: Switching which system is authoritative happens once, with a way back defined up front. Follow the observation window and the stabilise or roll back call.

seoTitle: Historical Backfill Without Replaying Stale Actions
seoDescription: Repairing a gap in the record without re-enacting what those events would have caused. See how the backfill window is scoped and then applied safely.

seoTitle: Data Transformation Error Recovery Journey Example
seoDescription: Undoing a wrong data change without undoing the right things that came after. Review the reconciliation and the correct, roll forward or roll back paths.

seoTitle: Decision Request Intake and Routing Journey Example
seoDescription: Establishes that authorised judgment is genuinely required and opens a case with a stated scope. Follow the validation and the route, reject or hold exits.

seoTitle: Assigning a Decision Case to an Authorised Reviewer
seoDescription: Putting a case in front of someone actually authorised to decide it. This flow makes reviewer ownership explicit and covers reassignment and escalation.

seoTitle: Evaluating Evidence to Reach an Authorised Decision
seoDescription: How sufficient evidence turns into an authorised decision inside the scope the reviewer holds, and when the case goes back for more information instead.

seoTitle: Collecting Missing Information Before a Decision
seoDescription: Pausing a decision for the fact it is actually missing, without losing the review already done. Follow the collect, revalidate and resume sequence here.

seoTitle: Approved Decision Execution and Revalidation Path
seoDescription: An authorisation still has to apply to what it was granted against. This flow revalidates the target at execution, then executes, holds or invalidates.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of DEC-188, which also revalidates an approval before use; DEC-185 revalidates the target at execution while DEC-188 tests the approval's own validity boundaries.

seoTitle: Recording a Rejection and the Requester's Options
seoDescription: Treats a refusal as the business outcome it is. The reason is recorded and the requester is pointed to remediation, to closure or to a route to reapply.

seoTitle: Splitting Scope After a Partial Approval Decision
seoDescription: Separates the authorised and unauthorised halves of one request so only the approved part can move, and shows how the remaining scope is then resolved.

seoTitle: Approval Validity, Expiry and Revalidation Journey
seoDescription: At the moment of use, is the approval still one? This flow revalidates it in time, context and count, then permits use, expires it or reopens the review.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of DEC-185, the approval execution journey; both gate an approval at the point of use, this one on the approval's own validity boundaries.

seoTitle: Decision Escalation to Higher Authority Journey Map
seoDescription: Shows how a stalled case moves to an authority that can actually resolve it, carrying the work already done forward without predetermining the outcome.

seoTitle: Reopening a Superseded Decision Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Models how a challenged or superseded decision is revalidated and then continued or replaced, with every part of the original record left as it was.
reviewReason: Near-identical subject to FBK-47 (appeal and dispute review): both model revisiting a decision that has already been made.

seoTitle: Create, Reuse or Waive a Document Journey Example
seoDescription: Walks through deciding whether a process needs a new artifact or whether one already exists that answers the requirement, and where each path ends.

seoTitle: Document Drafting and Validation Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Models how a draft is populated from authoritative sources and checked for completeness, so it reaches a ready or blocked state before anything is issued.

seoTitle: Document Issuance and Version Freeze Journey Map
seoDescription: Shows how an authorized document becomes an issued version that can be identified and referenced later, and that cannot be quietly changed after the fact.

seoTitle: Document Distribution and Delivery Journey Example
seoDescription: Traces how one issued version reaches the party who should have it, by send or by access, keeping delivery confirmation and failure separate from issuance.

seoTitle: Document Signature Collection Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Models collecting every required signature against one exact document version, and how the signed, declined and expired outcomes are told apart.

seoTitle: When a Signed Document Becomes Effective Journey Map
seoDescription: Models the gap between signing and taking effect, showing how completion is validated and when a document is effective or held by a pending condition.

seoTitle: Document Amendment and Versioning Journey Example
seoDescription: Shows how an issued artifact is changed by creating a successor that supersedes it going forward, leaving the version it replaces exactly as it was.

seoTitle: Document Expiry and Renewal Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Covers what happens when a time-limited document reaches expiry, revalidating the requirement and choosing renew, replace or close for dependent work.

seoTitle: Document Revocation and Withdrawal Journey Map
seoDescription: Models withdrawing an artifact on an authority's decision, ending future reliance as far as that decision reaches and reconciling what depended on it.

seoTitle: Conflicting Document Versions Journey Example
seoDescription: Shows how the version that actually governs is determined when records disagree, and how the conflict is explained and reconciled instead of being deleted.

seoTitle: Feedback Request Eligibility Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Models deciding whether asking for feedback is appropriate at all, and holding the gap between the ask and the response as a real state with its own exits.

seoTitle: Customer Advocacy Eligibility Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Models asking someone to vouch for you only where the relationship has actually earned it, and keeping permission for public reuse as a separate decision.

seoTitle: Feedback Routing and Loop Closure Journey Map
seoDescription: Traces how received feedback is classified and routed to the process that can act on it, and stays open until anything promised in return has happened.

seoTitle: Negative Feedback Issue Check Customer Journey
seoDescription: Checks whether an unresolved obligation genuinely exists behind negative feedback before any recovery starts, then resolves, acknowledges or escalates it.

seoTitle: Positive Feedback and Recognition Journey Example
seoDescription: Records a good experience as evidence and acknowledges the person, keeping any advocacy opportunity a separate decision rather than an automatic next step.

seoTitle: Complaint Ownership and Issue Closure Journey Flow
seoDescription: Holds an actionable issue as an open obligation with a named owner, and closes it only once both the fix and the agreed closure condition are satisfied.

seoTitle: Customer Appeal and Dispute Review Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Models reviewing a decision that has already been made, with uphold, reverse and modify outcomes and the original left standing while the review runs.
reviewReason: Near-identical subject to DEC-190 (decision reconsideration): both model revisiting a decision that has already been made.

seoTitle: Declared Preference Recalculation Journey Map
seoDescription: Shows how something a person tells you about their situation is stored and then reaches only the decisions that genuinely depend on it, and nothing else.

seoTitle: Missing Critical Data Resolution Journey Example
seoDescription: Treats a blocking data gap as a named dependency to request or resolve before work resumes, kept distinct from simply wanting to know more about someone.

seoTitle: Relationship Signals and Evidence Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Accumulates relationship signals as dated evidence and reassesses state, allowing a relationship label only where a policy has defined what it means.

seoTitle: Financial Obligation Lifecycle Journey Example
seoDescription: Holds what is owed as its own state from creation through due to satisfied or outstanding, independent of any attempt to pay it or message sent about it.

seoTitle: Payment Attempt and Outcome Routing Journey Map
seoDescription: Separates initiating a payment from knowing what happened to it, routing each attempt to success, failure or an explicit unknown-outcome state.

seoTitle: Authorization, Capture and Settlement Journey Flow
seoDescription: Models the commitment of funds as three states, where reserving, taking and receiving money each hold their own state through to settlement or release.

seoTitle: Failed Payment Recovery Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Classifies why a payment actually failed and answers that specific reason, choosing recovery, an alternate route or exit while the obligation stays alive.

seoTitle: Unknown Payment Outcome Reconciliation Journey Map
seoDescription: Establishes what really happened to a payment whose outcome was lost, confirming success or failure before the customer is charged for that attempt again.
reviewReason: Overlaps with FIN-140 (financial reconciliation) on reconciliation search intent; the scopes differ (one payment attempt vs disagreeing record sets) and need separate positioning.

seoTitle: Obligation Satisfaction and Balance Journey Example
seoDescription: Applies a financial event to an obligation exactly once, reconciles the balance and releases only the state that genuinely depended on that obligation.

seoTitle: Refund Request and Eligibility Decision Journey
seoDescription: Turns a refund request into an authorised approve, reject or review decision, with no money moving on the strength of the request itself at any point.

seoTitle: Refund Execution and Confirmation Journey Map
seoDescription: Moves an approved refund and confirms that it arrived, held deliberately apart from the earlier decision that the refund should be issued at all.

seoTitle: Financial Dispute and Chargeback Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Runs a transaction-level dispute through the authority that decides it, gathering evidence and reconciling it without treating the claim as a finding.

seoTitle: Financial Reconciliation and Mismatch Journey Map
seoDescription: Detects a material mismatch across financial records, then explains and corrects the difference or escalates it, never by editing the awkward record.
reviewReason: Overlaps with FIN-135 (unknown payment reconciliation) on reconciliation search intent; the scopes differ (disagreeing record sets vs one payment attempt) and need separate positioning.

seoTitle: Fulfillment Request Acceptance Journey Example
seoDescription: Decides whether you are taking responsibility for delivering something, holding accept, reject and hold as states distinct from simply having been asked.

seoTitle: Fulfillment Availability and Allocation Journey Map
seoDescription: Establishes whether the resources to satisfy an accepted obligation exist in the scope and window that serves it, then allocates, backorders or rejects.

seoTitle: Resource Allocation and Reservation Journey Map
seoDescription: Binds specific capacity to one fulfillment obligation until it is consumed or deliberately let go, with confirm, release and reallocate paths.

seoTitle: Fulfillment Execution and Completion Journey Map
seoDescription: Tracks how much of an obligation's scope has been satisfied, so complete, partial and failed outcomes reflect delivery, not an internal step's report.

seoTitle: Fulfillment Exception Handling Journey Example
seoDescription: Diagnoses an operational problem and changes only the part of the obligation it actually touches, routing to recovery, substitution or a failed outcome.

seoTitle: Fulfillment Delay and Reschedule Journey Example
seoDescription: How a late fulfillment is held as its own state, with the original commitment still intact behind it, then routed to continue, reschedule or escalate.

seoTitle: Dispatch and Delivery Tracking Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: A flow that hands execution to whoever performs the delivery while the obligation stays open and ours, tracking it to delivered, failed or unknown.

seoTitle: Failed Delivery Attempt Recovery Journey Example
seoDescription: Recovering a failed delivery according to why it failed, inside a bounded number of attempts. Review the retry, correction, alternate and return paths.

seoTitle: Delivery Acceptance and Finalization Journey Map
seoDescription: Arriving and being agreed to have arrived correctly are different facts here. Follow the confirmation, the issue window and the route to finalization.

seoTitle: Fulfillment Cancellation Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Stopping what remains of an obligation while keeping everything that already happened. See how completed, in-progress and unstarted work are separated.

seoTitle: Identity Claim Verification Journey Example
seoDescription: How confidence is established in one specific identity claim and bound to the evidence behind it, ending in verified, rejected or more evidence needed.

seoTitle: Verification Dependency and Process Unblock Journey
seoDescription: A verification requirement held as its own state, blocking only the process that needs it and releasing that process only once everything is rechecked.

seoTitle: Document Submission and Validation Journey Map
seoDescription: Uploading a document and satisfying a requirement stay separate facts. Follow validation to accept, reject or replace, bound to the requirement assessed.

seoTitle: Verification Failure Routing Customer Journey Map
seoDescription: Routing a failed verification by the reason it failed, and keeping internal errors out of the customer record. Retry, remediate, review or exit branches.

seoTitle: Authentication Challenge Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Establishing that whoever is present controls the required identity, at the assurance the context demands. See the authenticate, step up and deny exits.

seoTitle: Step-Up Authentication Journey Map for Sensitive Actions
seoDescription: Raising identity assurance before a sensitive action runs, then confirming the action is still authorised. Follow the resume and deny branches in full.
reviewReason: Subject overlaps materially with IDN-85 (authentication challenge); both cover authenticating an actor with a step-up or deny outcome and may compete on the same query.

seoTitle: Authentication Failure Pattern and Recovery Journey
seoDescription: Telling an ordinary forgotten password apart from an account under attack, without turning the first into the second. Security check, recover or restrict.

seoTitle: Account Recovery and Access Restoration Journey Map
seoDescription: A way back into an account someone can no longer authenticate to, built so the recovery route is never weaker than the access it replaces. Prove control.

seoTitle: Identity Attribute Change and Propagation Journey
seoDescription: Changing an identity attribute safely, then reconciling everything that relied on the old value independently instead of letting it inherit the new one.

seoTitle: Suspected Account Compromise Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Limiting what a possible compromise could do while the question is open, then reaching a conclusion that can clear the account or move it into recovery.

seoTitle: Incident Correlation and Confirmation Journey Map
seoDescription: Deciding whether several failures really share one cause before they are treated as a single incident. Follow the candidate to confirmation or rejection.

seoTitle: Incident Severity and Blast Radius Journey Map
seoDescription: Once an incident is confirmed, this flow establishes what is affected, how badly it is affected, and who owns and runs the operational response.

seoTitle: Incident Containment and Mitigation Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Reducing damage now without pretending the cause is dealt with. See how containment, mitigation and the protection of critical operations are held apart.

seoTitle: Incident Communication and Status Update Journey
seoDescription: Identifying the cohort actually affected and telling them something true and useful through the mechanism that already owns delivery. Inform or update.

seoTitle: Root Cause Investigation and Corrective Action Journey
seoDescription: Testing hypotheses until one actually explains the incident rather than the one nearest to it. Follow confirm, reject and corrective action branches.

seoTitle: Incident Recovery and Verification Journey Example
seoDescription: Acting on the cause, then checking the affected population instead of a command's return code. Examine the restore, verify and continue paths in the flow.

seoTitle: Recovery Observation Window Journey Example
seoDescription: Holding an incident open long enough to know the recovery actually held. This flow models the observation window and the split between stable and relapse.

seoTitle: Incident Resolution and Residual Case Handling Journey
seoDescription: Closing a shared failure without closing the individual problems it caused. See how linked cases and obligations survive the end of the response.

seoTitle: Post-Incident Review and Corrective Work Journey
seoDescription: Turning what an incident revealed into corrective work that somebody owns and somebody verifies. Follow the review, assignment and verification sequence.

seoTitle: Recurring Incident Pattern and Prevention Journey
seoDescription: Noticing when the same weakness keeps producing incidents instead of treating each one as new, then escalating prevention for the whole related family.

seoTitle: Integration Connection and Activation Journey Map
seoDescription: An integration becomes active only once it has proven it can do the thing it exists for, not once a credential is saved. Authenticate, validate, activate.

seoTitle: Integration Authorization Change Journey Example
seoDescription: Rechecking what an integration can still do whenever its authorization changes, rather than assuming valid credentials mean access stayed the same.

seoTitle: Integration Health Degradation Diagnosis Journey
seoDescription: Scoping a deteriorating integration to what is actually failing, with recovery established by evidence rather than by a metric returning to normal.

seoTitle: Pending External Operation Outcome Journey Map
seoDescription: Submitting an external operation and completing one stay separate states here, and an unknown outcome is allowed to remain unknown. Confirm, fail, unknown.

seoTitle: External Outcome Reconciliation Journey Example
seoDescription: Applying an external outcome to local state only after checking that it belongs here, has not already been applied, and still describes what is true.

seoTitle: Integration Failure Containment and Restore Journey
seoDescription: Halting work into an integration that cannot function, while keeping enough state to recover without repeating anything the provider may already have done.

seoTitle: Blocked Work Queue and Controlled Resume Journey
seoDescription: Keeping work that a failed integration blocked, but only where it can later be revalidated and safely resumed. Follow the hold, recover and resume path.

seoTitle: Integration Reconnect and Backfill Journey Map
seoDescription: Closing the gap an outage left in what is known, without recreating everything that would have happened had the events arrived on time. Backfill, dedupe.

seoTitle: Synchronization Conflict and Authority Rule Journey
seoDescription: Settling a cross-system disagreement with an explicit authority rule, and holding the record rather than guessing where no such rule exists for the fields.

seoTitle: External Dependency Outage and Degradation Journey
seoDescription: Losing only the capability that genuinely depends on an unavailable provider, while every uncertain outcome is left uncertain. Alternate route or recover.
reviewReason: Subject overlaps materially with INT-113 (integration health degradation) and INT-116 (integration failure); all three model losing and recovering an integration capability.

seoTitle: Async Work Lifecycle Journey from Queue to Completion
seoDescription: Explicit states for asynchronous work so accepting it, holding it, running it and finishing it are never read as one event. Complete and fail branches.

seoTitle: Queue Lag Prioritisation and Scaling Journey Map
seoDescription: Responding to a queue that cannot keep up, judged by how old the unfinished work is rather than by its volume. Prioritise, scale or degrade the workload.

seoTitle: Stalled Work Detection and Recovery Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Separates work that is merely slow from work that has stopped. Follow the progress-threshold trigger, the safe recovery checks and the escalation exits.

seoTitle: Retryable Failure Backoff, Retry and Exhaust Journey
seoDescription: Models how a transient failure is repeated inside a bounded budget. Examine the backoff waits, the safety conditions and the resolve or exhaust exits.

seoTitle: Duplicate Work Detection and Deduplication Journey Map
seoDescription: Stops one logical operation running twice while two legitimate repeats stay separate. Trace detection and the reuse, suppress and reconcile routes.

seoTitle: Partial Processing Failure Recovery Journey Example
seoDescription: A composite job ends with mixed outcomes: completed child work is preserved and only the failed scope is retried. See how each child is judged separately.

seoTitle: Dead-Letter Queue Diagnosis and Remediation Journey Map
seoDescription: Turns work automation could not finish into an obligation someone owns. Walk the diagnosis step and the replay, correct or close exits with their waits.

seoTitle: Worker Failure Recovery and Work Reclaim Journey Map
seoDescription: Moves execution off an unavailable worker without assuming the work failed or letting two workers hold it. Review the reclaim timing and the resume logic.

seoTitle: Backlog Recovery and Controlled Drain Journey Example
seoDescription: Once capacity returns, the backlog is inventoried by workload class, stale items are discarded and the rest is paced. Follow the revalidation steps.

seoTitle: Technical Success to Business Outcome Verification Journey
seoDescription: Technical success is not proof the intended state exists. See how the business entity is checked after a job reports success, then finalized or reconciled.

seoTitle: New Work Routing to Responsibility Scope Journey Map
seoDescription: Routes a new case, lead, task or request into the smallest genuinely valid responsibility scope, and stops where policy is silent. See the routing rules.

seoTitle: Assignment to Accepted Responsibility Journey Example
seoDescription: Proposed responsibility and accepted responsibility stay separate states, so work nobody has taken stays visible. Follow the acceptance wait and reminders.

seoTitle: Owner Assignment and Context Transfer Journey Example
seoDescription: A new owner receives what they need to continue an existing obligation, not just a record carrying their name. Trace the handover before work starts.
reviewReason: Subject overlaps closely with OWN-54: both cover handing an active entity to a new owner. This page is the context handover after an assignment becomes effective; OWN-54 is the authoritative ownership change and obligation transfer.

seoTitle: Ownership Change and Obligation Transfer Journey Example
seoDescription: Responsibility for an active entity moves while open obligations, running clocks and the record of earlier work stay intact. Review each transfer check.
reviewReason: Subject overlaps closely with OWN-53: both cover handing an active entity to a new owner. This page is the authoritative ownership change and obligation transfer; OWN-53 is the context handover after an assignment becomes effective.

seoTitle: Responsibility Escalation to Higher Authority Journey
seoDescription: Raises a blocker to the level that can clear it, without the original owner putting the work down by escalating. Follow the conditions and return path.

seoTitle: Approval Request, Review and Decision Journey Example
seoDescription: Binds an approval to the exact version reviewed and keeps approving separate from doing. Examine the approve, reject and request-changes branches.

seoTitle: Multi-Party Approval Decision Aggregation Journey Map
seoDescription: Combines several independent approval decisions strictly under the governing policy, and refuses to proceed where none defines how. See each decision held.

seoTitle: Material Change After Approval Impact Check Journey
seoDescription: When an approved subject changes before execution, this flow tests whether the approval still covers it and reopens only the decisions that no longer hold.

seoTitle: Rejected Approval and Resubmission Journey Example
seoDescription: Rejection is neither a dead end nor an open retry loop. Follow the revision eligibility check, the resubmit route and the block on a rejected version.

seoTitle: Decision Authority Change and Revalidation Journey Map
seoDescription: Pending decisions are revalidated against who is authorized now, without unapproving history or moving items blindly. See the transfer and continue routes.

seoTitle: Entity Relationship Creation and Validation Journey
seoDescription: A link between two entities activates only where the relationship has an authoritative basis. See the validation, the reject exit and why it stays a link.

seoTitle: Relationship Change and Rights Recalculation Journey
seoDescription: When a relationship changes, exactly what depended on it is recalculated and nothing else. Trace which rights and obligations are re-evaluated in the flow.

seoTitle: Relationship End and Obligation Reconciliation Journey
seoDescription: Ending a relationship stops what it carried forward without cancelling what it validly produced. Follow the dependency removal and reconciliation steps.

seoTitle: Role Change Authority and Capability Delta Journey Map
seoDescription: Applies the difference between an old and a new role, so what a member may do next moves while what they did under the old role is left undisturbed.

seoTitle: Parent State Change Propagation to Child Records Journey
seoDescription: A parent's state change reaches only the children that genuinely depend on it. Each child is checked against a written dependency rule first.

seoTitle: Parent State Aggregation From Child States Journey
seoDescription: Recomputes a parent's state from the full set of children the policy reads, rather than following whichever child reported last. See the aggregation logic.

seoTitle: Duplicate Entity Detection and Assessment Journey Example
seoDescription: Assesses whether two records represent the same entity and routes the answer to keep separate, link or merge, without consolidating anything here.

seoTitle: Entity Linking With Independent Identity Journey Map
seoDescription: Records that two entities are related and lets defined context cross between them while both remain separate entities. Review the self-contained flow.

seoTitle: Entity Split and History Allocation Journey Example
seoDescription: Separates what should never have been one record, allocating state and history safely without copying the things that do not divide. See each step.

seoTitle: Orphaned Entity Detection and Resolution Journey Map
seoDescription: A missing required relationship becomes an explicit, findable state instead of a null field active work runs against. Follow both resolution routes.

seoTitle: Post-Completion Issue Validation and Remedy Route Journey
seoDescription: Establishes whether something delivered has left an obligation unresolved, then routes it to a recovery mechanism that could satisfy it. See the checks.

seoTitle: Return Request Eligibility and Authorization Journey
seoDescription: Decides whether an item may enter a return process, apart from whether money is owed. Examine the eligibility rules, the review branch and the reject exit.

seoTitle: Authorized Return in Transit Tracking Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Tracks whether an authorized return actually comes back, holding the in-transit, received, lost and expired states. Follow the waits and the handoff.

seoTitle: Returned Item Inspection and Acceptance Journey Map
seoDescription: Judges what came back against the conditions it was authorized under, keeping receipt and acceptance apart. See the accept, reject and partial routes.

seoTitle: Replacement Remedy Allocation and Fulfillment Journey
seoDescription: Delivers a second time against the same promise, tied to the defect it exists to resolve. Walk the allocation, fulfillment and confirmation steps.

seoTitle: Correction and Reperformance Verification Journey Example
seoDescription: Produces the outcome that should have been produced while the record still shows the first one was wrong. Follow the execution and verification steps.

seoTitle: Remedy Selection and Obligation Resolution Journey
seoDescription: Chooses the remedy that would genuinely satisfy an unresolved obligation, from the options that exist, with a financial handoff where one is needed.

seoTitle: Remedy Outcome Verification and Closure Journey Example
seoDescription: Checks that a remedy satisfied the obligation rather than that it was carried out. See the verification wait and the close or continue-recovery exits.

seoTitle: Compensation Eligibility, Decision and Delivery Journey
seoDescription: Decides separately whether impact warrants more than fixing the problem, then confirms it arrived. Follow eligibility, grant or reject, and delivery.

seoTitle: Post-Remedy Issue Recurrence Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: A journey for problems reported after a remedy: it separates a true recurrence from a new issue or an unfinished fix, then routes each to its own path.

seoTitle: Engagement State Reclassification Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Engagement moves in both directions. See how a changed engagement state is reclassified, and how the flow decides if the move is worth acting on.

seoTitle: Missed Expected Usage Check Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: What happens when an expected usage milestone is missed: the flow first checks that an expectation existed and that another signal corroborates it.

seoTitle: Health Deterioration Diagnosis Lifecycle Journey Map
seoDescription: When a health state crosses a deterioration threshold, this journey diagnoses the mechanism breaking the relationship and routes to a matching recovery.

seoTitle: Churn Risk Escalation and Evidence Journey Example
seoDescription: How a crossed churn risk threshold escalates: the flow weighs independent evidence and sets intervention priority in proportion to what it supports.

seoTitle: Negative Experience Recovery Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Recovery logic after a confirmed negative experience: what failed, whether it is fixed, and whether a remedy is genuinely owed before any response.

seoTitle: Recovery Signal Observation Buffer Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: A positive signal is not yet a recovery. This journey holds an observation window after improvement so a relapse is still watched for when it happens.

seoTitle: Cancellation Intent Decision Point Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Stated intent to leave handled as a decision point: read the current state, offer a genuinely relevant alternative, or let the cancellation proceed.

seoTitle: Completed Cancellation Wind-Down Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Once a cancellation is authoritative, retention ownership ends. See how the flow stops retention and resolves what is still outstanding afterwards.

seoTitle: Retention Intervention Outcome and Exit Journey Map
seoDescription: Closing a retention attempt on what actually happened to the relationship: suppress, escalate or exit, with logic that stops the same offer twice.

seoTitle: Change Rollout Eligibility Gate Journey Map Example
seoDescription: Before any target is prepared, this journey decides which targets a change may reach at all, evaluating each against it and marking it ready or blocked.

seoTitle: Change Preparation and Dependency Resolution Journey
seoDescription: How an eligible target is brought into a state where the change can actually be applied, resolving dependencies and holding it when they are unmet.

seoTitle: Scheduled Change Wait and Revalidation Journey Map
seoDescription: A scheduled change is not always still the right one. The flow waits for the execution window, revalidates against the target, then executes or cancels.

seoTitle: Change Execution and State Verification Journey Map
seoDescription: Applying a change to one target and establishing that it ended in the intended state, with verified, failed and unknown outcomes handled separately.

seoTitle: Staged Rollout Cohort and Health Gate Journey Example
seoDescription: A staged rollout that widens only when the cohort already carrying the change shows it is safe, with a health gate between each expansion step.

seoTitle: Rollout Pause, Diagnose and Resume Journey Example
seoDescription: Freezing an expansion while the decision is open: the flow stops the change spreading, diagnoses it, then resumes, rolls back or ends the rollout.

seoTitle: Rollback or Forward Recovery Decision Journey Example
seoDescription: When a change failure threshold is reached, this router settles whether going back is safer than going forward before any rollback work begins.

seoTitle: Rollback Execution and Stability Verification Flow
seoDescription: Returning affected targets to a known-good state and proving they actually work there, with the restore steps and the stability check laid out end to end.

seoTitle: Individual Target Change Failure Recovery Journey Map
seoDescription: Recovering a single target that could not take the change through retry, isolation or remediation, and noticing when it stops being one isolated target.

seoTitle: Change Completion and Observation Window Journey Map
seoDescription: After the planned population reaches the changed state, the flow observes long enough to know the change held, keeping recovery material until then.

seoTitle: Policy Check Evaluation Journey: Pass, Block or Review
seoDescription: How a protected action is evaluated against the rules that actually govern it, at the applicable policy version, then routed to pass, block or review.

seoTitle: Risk Signal Evidence Correlation Journey Map Example
seoDescription: Turning a risk measurement into a state change no larger than its evidence supports, with clear, monitor, restrict and review paths that expire.

seoTitle: Scoped Risk Restriction and Release Journey Example
seoDescription: Restricting the smallest thing that manages the risk while keeping a stated route back, with review and release paths mapped beside the restriction.

seoTitle: Policy Violation Detection and Validation Journey Map
seoDescription: Establishing that a rule was actually broken, judged against the policy version that governed it, before correction, restriction or escalation.

seoTitle: Compliance Requirement Verification Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: One mandatory requirement held as its own state: the flow collects and verifies what it needs, and blocks only the processes that genuinely depend on it.

seoTitle: Compliance or Policy Hold, Resume or Terminate Journey
seoDescription: Pausing only what a policy question makes unsafe while everything else keeps running, preserving state until the hold resolves or the work is ended.

seoTitle: Policy Exception Request and Authority Check Journey
seoDescription: Asking for a controlled deviation from a named rule over a stated scope: the journey validates who may ask, then approves, rejects or sends to review.

seoTitle: Approved Exception Scoped Override Journey Example
seoDescription: Letting an authorized deviation apply exactly where it was authorized, invoked action by action, and stopping the moment it expires or is revoked.

seoTitle: Limit or Quota Reached Customer Journey Map Example
seoDescription: A limit being reached treated as the limit working: the flow gives the constrained action a real path forward through waiting, an increase or reset.

seoTitle: Policy or Risk State Change Propagation Journey Map
seoDescription: Re-evaluating affected work when a policy or risk state changes, applying the new authority only where it reaches and leaving past decisions alone.

seoTitle: Availability Query and Capacity Check Journey Example
seoDescription: Answering an availability request with options genuinely bookable right now, while saying plainly that nothing is being held for the person asking.

seoTitle: Temporary Slot Hold and Release Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Protecting specific capacity for a bounded moment while a booking is completed, then confirming, expiring or releasing it without calling it a booking.

seoTitle: Reservation Request Validation Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Turning a request for a specific time into a commitment both sides can rely on, with validation and clear confirmed, rejected and pending outcomes.

seoTitle: Confirmed Reservation Preparation Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: After a booking is confirmed, this journey puts the conditions for a successful service in place without letting preparation move the promised time.

seoTitle: Reschedule Request and Availability Recheck Journey
seoDescription: Moving a booked commitment to a new time: recheck availability, then move, reject or preserve the original so the customer never holds neither one.

seoTitle: Reservation Cancellation Customer Journey Map Example
seoDescription: Ending a future time commitment cleanly: stop the commitment, return the capacity to the schedule, and leave the money side to be decided in another flow.

seoTitle: Scheduled Start Revalidation Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: As the start window approaches, the booking is revalidated as it stands now rather than as confirmed weeks ago, then routed to check-in or exception.

seoTitle: Appointment Attendance and Completion Journey Example
seoDescription: A journey that separates someone turning up from whether the service was actually delivered, splitting into complete, partial and interrupted endings.

seoTitle: Appointment No-Show and Rebooking Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: How a confirmed booking is established as a genuine no-show once other explanations are ruled out, then routed to rebooking, closure or a consequence.

seoTitle: Provider Cancellation and Rebooking Journey Example
seoDescription: Models recovering a booking the provider or resource cannot fulfil, reallocating it so no cost falls on the customer who was ready to be served.

seoTitle: Subscription and Contract Creation Journey Example
seoDescription: Shows why a subscription, contract or policy existing is not the same as it running, with validation deciding between an active and a pending start.

seoTitle: Future-Dated Subscription Activation Journey Example
seoDescription: A future-dated agreement waits until its effective time, then activates on what is true at that moment rather than on what was true when it was set up.

seoTitle: Subscription Renewal Decision Window Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Examine how a renewal window reaches a decision about the next term as a decision only, checking eligibility and routing to renew, non-renew or review.

seoTitle: Subscription Renewal Execution and New Term Journey
seoDescription: What has to be true before a new term actually exists: this flow runs the financial and dependency checks that a renewal decision alone cannot settle.

seoTitle: Failed Renewal Payment and Grace Period Journey Map
seoDescription: What should a subscription do while a failed renewal payment is chased? This flow holds the relationship open, then routes it to renewal or to a lapse.

seoTitle: Subscription Plan or Terms Change Request Journey Map
seoDescription: A change requested on a running subscription is validated, then scheduled, applied or rejected, always as a delta against the terms in force at the time.

seoTitle: Subscription Cancellation Request Journey Example
seoDescription: Works out whether and when a relationship ends while the current term keeps running, choosing between a scheduled end date and cancelling immediately.

seoTitle: Scheduled Cancellation Revalidation Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: A scheduled end is rechecked at its effective time, so a subscription the customer has since decided to keep is preserved rather than closed by a timer.

seoTitle: Subscription Suspension and Hold Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Models holding a relationship in a state where it cannot operate normally and has not ended, then deciding whether it is restored or brought to an end.

seoTitle: Subscription End and Final Reconciliation Journey
seoDescription: At the end of a continuing relationship, this flow stops what it was granting while everything it created carries on through its own separate lifecycle.

seoTitle: Deadline Tracking, Escalation and Expiry Journey Map
seoDescription: Here a deadline governs the state of a single obligation instead of scheduling messages around a date, ending in completion, escalation or expiry.

seoTitle: Obligation Due and Overdue State Change Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: When an obligation becomes due or overdue, this flow changes what it costs operationally rather than only announcing it, then resolves or escalates.

seoTitle: Pre-Expiry Eligibility Window Customer Journey Example
seoDescription: Uses the window before an expiry only where acting inside it could change the outcome, with an eligibility check before renewing, completing or expiring.

seoTitle: Expiry Execution and Current State Validation Journey
seoDescription: At the moment an expiry fires, the entity is rechecked against the version the timer was written for, then expired, extended or replaced accordingly.

seoTitle: Grace Period and Temporary Continuity Journey Example
seoDescription: Keeps limited continuity while something recoverable is still unresolved, without pretending the normal active state survives, then recovers or terminates.

seoTitle: Temporary Exception and Validity Window Journey Map
seoDescription: Stops an exception granted for a reason from quietly becoming permanent: it runs on a validity window that ends in a revert or in a formalised change.

seoTitle: Temporary State Expiry and Restore Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Gives any time-bound state placed on an entity a defined ending, and revalidates before anything is returned to what it was or moved on to a new state.
reviewReason: Subject overlaps TIM-66 (temporary-exception): both model a time-bound state ending in revert or transition; TIM-67 is the generic case, TIM-66 the granted-exception case. Confirm the two pages stay distinct.

seoTitle: Reversible Transition and Reversal Window Journey Map
seoDescription: A transition can be undone inside its reversal window, restoring only the side effects that are independently still valid, or confirmed once time runs out.

seoTitle: Post-Expiry Re-Entry and Requalification Journey Example
seoDescription: How something already expired can become valid again through the mechanism that genuinely restores validity, by renewing, requalifying or staying expired.

seoTitle: Scheduled Future Transition Execution Journey Map
seoDescription: Treats a scheduled transition as an intention recorded in the past and checks it against the present, then applies, cancels or recalculates it.

seoTitle: Identity and Entity Merge Execution Journey Example
seoDescription: Records that represent one entity are consolidated only after every dependent state has been reconciled under its own authority rule, then verified.

seoTitle: Merge Conflict Detection and Resolution Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: What a merge should do when consolidating would mean inventing an authority nobody holds: move to a safe state, resolve the conflict, continue or abort.

seoTitle: Account Consolidation and Dependency Journey Example
seoDescription: Unifies business structure across several accounts while every person involved stays a separate person, reconciling dependencies into one relationship.

seoTitle: Primary Relationship Transfer and Dependency Journey
seoDescription: Moves a dependent entity to a new primary after validating it, carrying across only the things the primary relationship actually governs and nothing more.

seoTitle: Role and Responsibility Handover Journey Example
seoDescription: A role passes between two people at one defined moment, with nothing before the handover changed and nothing behind it rewritten as the work continues.

seoTitle: Account Closure Request and Blocker Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: An account relationship ends once the obligations that legitimately block it are resolved, and nothing beyond that account is ended along with it.

seoTitle: Account Closure External Dependency Reconciliation Journey
seoDescription: While a closure finalises, each external and commercial dependency is reconciled on its own, so nothing outside the account is assumed to have ended too.

seoTitle: Post-Closure Account Wind-Down Lifecycle Journey Map
seoDescription: After a closure succeeds, normal account activity stops while the obligations that outlive it are allowed to finish, ending in a former or terminal state.

seoTitle: Data Deletion Request and Retention Scope Journey Map
seoDescription: Works out what a deletion request actually covers, then holds, deletes or keeps only the data an authoritative retention obligation genuinely requires.

seoTitle: Data Deletion Execution and Verification Journey Map
seoDescription: Carries an approved deletion through every system it must reach, verifying each one and keeping any part that did not arrive visible instead of assumed.
